function: Learned TDQN acts above the PHY: its actions are UAV 3D movements and TDMA GT scheduling (p. 7); RIS phases are computed by alignment, not learned (p. 3).
notes: Exclude, above_phy, p. 7. The TDQN action is a(t) = {lt, ht, cu,n,t}: p. 7: "the lt, ht represent the movements of the UAV in the horizontal direction ... and in the vertical direction"; "The cu,n,t represents the scheduling decision of the GT n"; p. 10: "combined product of horizontal flight action, vertical flight action, and GT scheduling". UAV trajectory and scheduling are listed above the PHY. The RIS phase shift, the only PHY decision, is not learned: p. 3: "the planned UAV positions for each time slot are used to calculate the phase shift of the RIS"; p. 6: "aligning the UAV-RIS-GT link maximizes the signal gain"; Algorithm 2 line 10, "Design the RIS's phase shift", is a step outside the network (p. 9). The aerial-link exception does not apply: p. 5: "the transmission power of the UAV is fixed", bandwidth is fixed at 2 MHz (Table II, p. 10), and no beam is learned. K-DBSCAN is a non-learned clustering for UAV placement and movement range (pp. 6-7). no_learning not chosen: a learned method (TDQN) is the core of the work, but it acts above the PHY. Reviewer may confirm that learned TDMA user scheduling is scheduling rather than aerial resource allocation (the latter would make it area 6). Title and DOI on p. 1 match the assigned work.
